summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, gastroparesis, and recurrent abdominal pain flares was admitted for severe nausea, vomiting, and inability to tolerate oral intake. She presented in significant pain with elevated blood pressure and leukocytosis. IV fluids, antiemetics, and pain control were initiated, and a temporary femoral line was placed due to poor venous access. Over the hospital course, her pain and symptoms improved with standing metoclopramide and bethanechol. An MRCP showed no structural abnormalities, and additional testing ruled out rare causes such as heavy metal toxicity and mast cell disease. A double-lumen port was successfully placed for long-term venous access. Her hypertension was monitored, and she was discharged home with medication adjustments, instructions for port care, and plans for outpatient follow-up including a gastric emptying study and evaluation for IV iron.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
